title: k8s-helm-node-provisioning-debug-scratchpad-2
content:
Goal: collect breadcrumbs for the flaky node provisioning issue (nodes stuck NotReady / kubelet crashloops after bootstrap).

Context: New batch of CI and Dedicated-capacity nodes (g4dn-like) provisioned via cloud-init + k8s-bootstrap helm chart. Intermittent failures across multiple AZs. Symptoms vary: some nodes register then go NotReady, others fail to register at all, some have kube-proxy CrashLoopBackOff.

What I've tried (commands + outputs / notes):

1) Quick cluster view
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
  -> many nodes in Ready, but ~3 in NotReady (InternalIP shows, AGE 2m)

- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-3-45.ec2.internal
  Events:
    Normal  RegisteredNode  Node ip-10-0-3-45 registered
    Warning KubeletNotReady  kubelet is not ready
    Warning  FailedSync  Error syncing pod "kube-proxy-xxx": failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to set up sandbox container

2) kubelet journal on the node (ssh into instance)
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
  Jan 12 07:23:12 ip-10-0-3-45 kubelet[1234]: E012 07:23:12.345 kubelet.go:2195] node "ip-10-0-3-45" not found
  Jan 12 07:23:13 ip-10-0-3-45 kubelet[1234]: E012 07:23:13.678 kubelet_node_status.go:70] Failed to update node status: timed out waiting for the condition
  Jan 12 07:23:15 ip-10-0-3-45 kubelet[1234]: E012 07:23:15.901 remote_runtime.go:172] RunPodSandbox from runtime service failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to setup network for sandbox "...": CNI failed to set up pod "kube-proxy-xxx" network: error adding pod to network: failed to call CNI plugin: exit status 1

3) container runtime status
- sudo systemctl status containerd
  -> Active (running) but recent restarts (1-2 restarts)
- sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200 --no-pager
  -> some errors about failed to load plugin: failed to find overlayfs (kernel missing?) - investigate kernel config on custom AMI.

4) CNI logs (calico) on the node/pods - kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | grep calico
  calico-node-xxxxx   CrashLoopBackOff on some nodes

- kubectl logs calico-node-xxxxx -n kube-system --previous
  -> 2025-11-12T07:21:05Z ERROR felix/health  Could not start BPF dataplane: missing kernel features (bpf not available)

Hypothesis: Custom AMI doesn't have required kernel modules for Calico BPF mode or overlay support. Some nodes boot with older kernel variant (AMI mismatch across AZs).

5) Helm chart (k8s-bootstrap) install/upgrade attempts
- helm -n kube-system upgrade --install k8s-bootstrap ./charts/k8s-bootstrap -f values-ci.yml --wait --timeout 10m
  -> sometimes times out waiting for DaemonSet (calico) pods to be Ready

6) TLS/bootstrap issues seen in API server logs
- kubectl -n kube-system logs kube-controller-manager-xxxxx
  -> 2025-11-12T07:22:00Z E1101 bootstrap-token-controller: failed to sign csr: signing request timeout

Hypothesis: Controller rate limits or Rundeck job created many tokens that saturated controller -> some kubelets stuck waiting for CSR approval (we have auto-approve controller but may be overloaded).

7) Commands tried to recover nodes
- kubectl cordon ip-10-0-3-45
- kubectl drain ip-10-0-3-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  -> drain hangs because kube-proxy pod stuck creating sandbox
- sudo systemctl restart kubelet && sudo systemctl restart containerd
  -> sometimes node comes Ready after containerd restart (race).
- rm -rf /var/lib/cni/networks/*; systemctl restart kubelet (on node)
  -> some success but not reproducible.

8) Network-level tests
- curl -sv https://10.0.0.1:443 (from node) -> TLS handshake ok, can reach apiserver
- nc -vz apiserver.internal:6443 -> success
- curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ -> works (so instance metadata is reachable)

9) Disk / inode checks
- df -h -> plenty of disk
- df -i -> inode usage fine

10) kube-proxy specific
- kubectl logs kube-proxy-xxx -n kube-system
  -> E1101 failed to load iptables: permission denied (apparmor?) -> some nodes have stricter AMI defaults.

11) Recent changes that might correlate
- New AMI baked with containerd v1.8.0 and kernel 5.15. Some older nodes still on previous image.
- Calico switched to BPF mode in last release (faster, but requires kernel features).
- Helm chart update changed tolerations/taints for kube-proxy/cni which may interact with provisioning ordering.

Working theory summary:
- Root cause likely a combination of AMI/kernel mismatch and timing/order of system services during cloud-init (containerd/container runtime starts, kubelet bootstraps before CNI is ready or kernel lacks features). This leads to CNI plugin failing to set up sandbox -> kube-proxy and calico crash -> node remains NotReady.
- Secondary factor: CSR signing/controller overload in some bursts causing nodes to fail to register in time.

Next steps / experiments to run:
- Reproduce with a single problematic AMI in staging across multiple AZs (force same AMI).
- Revert Calico to non-BPF mode in staging (quick test) and see if nodes bootstrap consistently.
- Add a cloud-init sleep to ensure containerd fully initialized before kubelet starts (or adjust systemd ordering: kubelet.service Wants=containerd.service After=containerd.service).
- Add more verbose logs to kubelet and short-lived debug script that runs after boot to capture /var/log/messages, dmesg, and containerd logs.
- Temporarily increase controller-manager logging and check bootstrap token CSR queue to see if signing spikes coincide with failures.
- Add node-bootstrap helm chart readiness probe that waits for CNI readiness before marking job complete.

Quick commands to run next time a repro occurs (one-liners):
- ssh node "sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 50"
- ssh node "sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 50"
- kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | egrep 'calico|kube-proxy'
- kubectl logs -n kube-system <pod> --previous
- curl -s localhost:10250/spec | jq . (kubelet)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Check AMI bake logs for kernel config and containerd package version.
- Pin AMI in staging and run 20 nodes repro.
- Rollback calico BPF flag in values-ci.yml and run helm upgrade.
- Add instrumentation to onboarding job to emit step timestamps to S3 for postmortem.

Unresolved questions:
- Why do some AZs show different AMI (image drift)? Is bake job sometimes failing to snapshot correctly?
- Is there a transient network partition between kubelet and control plane during bootstrap that causes CSR backlog?

If I find a clear root cause, copy final notes to Confluence (CONFLUENCE-1234) and create a postmortem.

End of scratchpad (iterate).
